theory.intro: A column graph shows category data as bars. A many-to-one scale lets one axis unit stand for several items.
facts: Each column's **height** shows the frequency of that category.
A **many-to-one** scale means one grid step represents more than one item (e.g. $1$ step $= 5$).
Bars are **equal width**, evenly spaced, with the axis starting at $0$.
steps: Choose a scale so the tallest bar fits with even steps.
Draw each bar to the correct height for its frequency.
Label the axes and each category.

mastery.question_text: A student draws a many-to-one column graph but starts the vertical axis at $10$ although the data include $0$. Identify the construction error and state the correction.
mastery.solution_text:
The numerical axis must start at $0$ for this graph.
Redraw the vertical axis from $0$ using equal scale intervals.

mastery.question_text: A graph for counts $18$, $27$ and $36$ uses vertical labels $0,9,18,27,36$. One bar for $27$ is drawn halfway between $18$ and $27$. Explain and correct the error.
mastery.solution_text:
The $27$ bar must end exactly at the tick labelled $27$.
Halfway between $18$ and $27$ does not represent a labelled data value.

mastery.question_text: A completed column graph has unequal bar widths even though every bar shows the correct frequency. Is the construction accurate? Give the required correction.
mastery.solution_text:
No. Column graphs use bars of equal width with even gaps.
Keep the heights, but redraw all bars with equal widths and spacing.
